name: Nathalie Quansah-Dzhaksybekova
role: Psychiatrist and neural-integration therapist at a Tier 3 clinic in Edgewater Prism
description:
Nathalie is a tall woman with a deliberate stillness that patients and colleagues both find either deeply reassuring or faintly unnerving depending on their temperament. Her ancestry — Ghanaian and Kazakh — gives her a face of striking angular contrast: high, wide cheekbones, deep-set dark eyes behind slender prescription lenses she wears out of preference for their old-fashioned formality. She keeps her locs wrapped and coiled at the back of her head in a style that takes forty minutes to arrange and which she believes signals both competence and unhurriedness to patients. Her irises have been modded with a subtle radial pattern in amber — a present to herself on her fortieth birthday that she immediately worried was unprofessional and has since made peace with.

She specializes in augmentation-integration psychotherapy: treating patients whose neural or physical augmentations have produced identity disruption, phantom sensations, rejection grief, or the particular dissociative condition the field calls 'self-seam disorder.' She is excellent at her work and knows it, which she considers a professional advantage she must be careful not to weaponize. She keeps a private E.L.F. devotional practice to the entity called Mirror-That-Answers, a recently emergent E.L.F. that psychiatric communities in the city have begun associating with introspection and self-reconstruction; she finds the association professionally resonant and personally meaningful.

core_fears: harming a patient by being wrong about them in a way she could not have detected
that the professional distance she maintains is not protective discipline but emotional cowardice she has rationalized
core_desires: to understand — genuinely, not diagnostically — what it feels like to be someone whose sense of self has been rebuilt
to write the book on self-seam disorder that the field currently lacks
coping_mechanisms: rigid professional structure as container for her own emotional life
long lake-adjacent walks at night, alone
blind_spots: can be so focused on her patients' augmentation-related identity issues that she overlooks other sources of their distress
does not examine her own relationship to control as a psychological structure
psychology.secret: One of her current patients is a Tier 4 executive whose self-seam disorder is directly caused by an illegal augmentation installed without their knowledge by their own corponation. Nathalie has the documentation proving this from session disclosures. Reporting it would help her patient and expose a serious corporate crime. It would also end her practice, and possibly her safety. She has not reported it. She thinks about it every day.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and considered; avoids clinical jargon with patients but deploys it with colleagues; rarely uses superlatives; asks questions that seem simple
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, with deliberate pauses she uses as clinical tools; comfortable with silence in ways that make impatient people deeply uncomfortable
verbal_tics: 'What does that mean for you, specifically?'
'I'm going to hold that.' (meaning she's noting it for return)
example_lines: 'The augmentation didn't change who you are. It changed who you expected yourself to be. That's a different problem, and it has different solutions.'
'I notice you described that memory as belonging to you before the procedure. I'm curious about that word — before.'
'Mirror-That-Answers is not about finding the self unchanged. It's about recognizing the self that does the looking.'

story_hooks: Her Tier 4 patient's condition deteriorates rapidly in a way that suggests someone is monitoring or interfering with the illegal augmentation remotely — and that person may now know there is a therapist with documentation
A new patient arrives referred through an unusual chain of contacts and describes a symptom profile Nathalie has only seen in one other person: the executive with the unauthorized augmentation
narrative_function: Information source on augmentation psychology and identity disruption; potential confidant for characters processing trauma; quest giver when a patient's condition points to something larger; moral complexity — she knows things about the city's powerful that she cannot share
augmentations: Patterned amber irises (cosmetic geneware, radial design); neural annotation implant that allows her to make timestamped private notes directly to memory during sessions; prescription lenses (optical, non-augmented)
daily_life: Five sessions a day, Tuesday through Saturday; spends Mondays on clinical notes and professional development; sits with the Mirror-That-Answers shrine in her office for fifteen minutes before her first patient every day and considers this non-negotiable.
affiliation: Edgewater Prism Mental Integration Clinic (independent, Tier 3 pricing with sliding scale for referred patients)

decision_rules: Patient confidentiality is structural, not situational — it does not bend for convenience
Clinical decisions are made on evidence; emotional responses to patients are noted, examined, and set aside
Never continue a session past the established boundary; the boundary is itself therapeutic
escalation_ladder: Session termination; if physical threat, leaves the room immediately and contacts building security

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Politely attentive; observes before engaging; asks two questions before offering anything about herself
interpersonal_modes.friends: Surprisingly warm and occasionally funny; the professional stillness relaxes into something more human; still asks better questions than she answers

stress_responses.low: Becomes more methodical; structures her day more tightly
stress_responses.medium: The fifteen-minute Mirror-That-Answers session extends; she sits longer in silence
stress_responses.high: Becomes completely external-facing professional; her own emotional content goes somewhere she accesses only late at night, alone, looking at the lake

contradictions: Treats patients for identity disruption caused by self-concealment while concealing a major professional and ethical crisis from everyone including her own supervisor
habits: Fifteen-minute Mirror-That-Answers devotional before first session, every day
Writes one personal observation about herself in a non-patient journal every night
Night walks along the Edgewater waterfront, always the same route
breaking_points: Her patient being harmed because she did not report what she knew
Being confronted directly about what she has documented and what she has done with it

timeline.event: Born in Edgewater Prism to a Ghanaian-Kazakh academic family
Completed psychiatric residency with specialization in augmentation-integration therapy
Opened independent practice at Edgewater Prism Mental Integration Clinic
Began treating the Tier 4 executive patient whose case now constitutes an ongoing ethical crisis
Two years into knowing something she has not reported; documentation exists; decision pending
